title: tests(audit): add staging integration test harness for sensitive actions + required audit fields
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
Summary: Adds an end-to-end integration test harness that runs in staging, performs a small set of representative sensitive actions, and asserts that corresponding audit events are emitted and conform to the schema-v1 required fields. This is intended to catch regressions like missing code paths, broken actor/request propagation, and pipeline validation failures before they reach customers.

Motivation / context: We’ve had a few near-misses where an action was instrumented in one code path but not another (e.g., token rotation), and unit tests didn’t catch it because the missing event only shows up after gateway/service propagation and pipeline validation. This harness exercises the real stack (gateway -> service -> audit pipeline -> storage) and verifies: (1) an event exists, (2) event_name matches expected registry name, (3) required fields are present and non-empty, and (4) outcome/error semantics are consistent.

What this PR does: Introduces a new test module under integration/ that uses a dedicated staging test org/workspace to perform sensitive actions via public APIs, then queries the audit log pipeline’s query endpoint to find the matching event(s) using request_id correlation. The harness is designed to be deterministic and minimally invasive: it creates ephemeral resources (API keys / roles) and cleans up after itself.

Scope (initial actions covered): - API key lifecycle: create -> rotate -> revoke (covers request_id propagation from gateway + actor attribution) - RBAC: create role -> update permissions -> delete role (covers diff payload presence + target modeling)

Assertions (schema v1 required fields): For each event, the harness asserts the following are present and valid: event_name, schema_version, occurred_at, org_id, actor.type, actor.id (or actor.service when applicable), request_id, ip, user_agent, outcome.result, and target.* (where applicable). It also asserts that sensitive values are not present in the payload (no token/secret fields), and that outcome.error_code / outcome.error_message are empty on success.

Reliability / flake resistance: Audit log persistence/export is eventually consistent. The harness polls for up to 90s (configurable) with exponential backoff and uses request_id as the primary correlation key. If multiple events are found for a request_id, it filters by expected event_name and validates the newest one. The test fails with a detailed diagnostic message including the query used and the partial event payload (redacted) to make failures actionable.

Operationalization: - Adds a new CI job definition (staging-only) behind RUN_AUDITLOG_E2E=1. Default CI remains unchanged. - Adds a nightly schedule entry in the staging pipeline (separate follow-up will wire paging; for now it reports failures to #eng-security and #eng-sre).

Files / areas changed (high level): - integration/auditlog_harness/runner.ts: test runner and polling utilities - integration/auditlog_harness/actions/*.ts: action helpers (api keys, rbac) - integration/auditlog_harness/assertions.ts: schema-v1 required field checks + redaction checks - services/audit-log-pipeline/client/query_client.ts: small client wrapper used by tests (staging only) - .ci/jobs/staging-auditlog-e2e.yml: staging job definition and env var wiring - docs/engineering/audit-logging/e2e-harness.md: how to run locally against staging and how to add a new action

Illustrative snippet (polling + validation): The harness performs the action, captures request_id from the response headers, then: waitForEvent({ requestId, eventName, timeoutMs: 90000 }) -> assertRequiredFields(event) -> assertNoSecrets(event).

Test plan: - Ran locally against staging: RUN_AUDITLOG_E2E=1 pnpm test:integration:auditlog (passes) - Forced failure validation: temporarily broke expected event_name to verify diagnostics include request_id + last-seen events (works) - Verified cleanup: resources created under rwi-staging-audit-e2e org are deleted at end of run (verified in console)

Rollout / follow-ups: - Next actions to add: model rollout actions (ENG-2485) and Dedicated scaling (ENG-2486) once those endpoints are stable in staging. - Consider adding a “minimum fields only” mode to avoid tightly coupling to optional payloads.

Security notes: - Uses a dedicated staging service account with least-privilege roles limited to the test org. - Does not log full event payloads; diagnostics are redacted and capped.

Checklist: - [x] No secrets added to repo; staging creds sourced from CI secret store - [x] Harness uses dedicated test org/workspace and cleans up resources - [x] Assertions match schema-v1 required fields (ENG-2481) - [x] Adds docs for adding new actions/events - [x] CI job is opt-in via env var; default PR CI unaffected

Review conversation (highlights): Marcus Lin: “Please ensure we fail if ip/user_agent are missing. Those are required for enterprise evidence.” Author: “Done. Also added explicit assertion that these fields are present and non-empty for user-initiated actions, and allowed null only for service actors (documented).” Nadia Rahman: “Polling window should be tied to delivery lag SLO. 90s feels high; can we make it configurable and emit timing metrics?” Author: “Made timeout configurable via AUDITLOG_E2E_TIMEOUT_MS, default 90s; also logs per-step timings to the test output. I’ll add metrics wiring in a follow-up once the job is permanently scheduled.” Rafael Mendes: “Avoid querying via internal admin endpoints that might change; prefer the pipeline query client that matches production.” Author: “Switched to audit-log-pipeline query client wrapper; removed the ad-hoc endpoint. Added a small adapter with versioned request/response types.” Chloe Martin: “RBAC tests should not assume the console backend is present. Keep it API-only.” Author: “Agreed; RBAC changes are performed via rbac service API directly. No dependency on console.” Allison Grant: “Make sure the harness doesn’t normalize away failures (e.g., querying by time range only). request_id is the right key.” Author: “All event lookups are request_id-first; time-range fallback is only for debugging output.”

Commits: - test(integration): scaffold audit log e2e harness runner - test(integration): add api key sensitive action helpers + assertions - test(integration): add rbac role CRUD helpers + assertions - chore(ci): add staging auditlog e2e job (gated) - docs: add auditlog e2e harness usage + contribution notes

CI: build (pass), lint (pass), unit tests (pass), integration:staging-auditlog-e2e (pass)

Merge: Squash merged into main.
